title: An activity in progress: singular object
summary: Choose singular partitive when describing an activity in progress without asserting completion.
targetSkills: An activity in progress: singular object
objectives: Choose singular partitive when describing an activity in progress without asserting completion.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose singular partitive when describing an activity in progress without asserting completion.
The partitive keeps the endpoint open. It does not say the task can never finish. Nyt makes the present activity explicit in these examples.
The complete verb and object forms are provided. The full system of total objects is deferred.
keyPoints: Partitive presents the action as an ongoing activity without asserting that the whole task is completed.

examples.english: I am reading a book now.
steps: Partitive presents the action as an ongoing activity without asserting that the whole task is completed.
Luen means “I am reading” and works as the verb. luen comes from lukea: lue- + -n, with k disappearing from luke-.
nyt means “now” and works as the time word. nyt is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
kirjaa means “book” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.

examples.english: I am reading a newspaper now.
steps: Partitive presents the action as an ongoing activity without asserting that the whole task is completed.
Luen means “I am reading” and works as the verb. luen comes from lukea: lue- + -n, with k disappearing from luke-.
nyt means “now” and works as the time word. nyt is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
lehteä means “newspaper” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Change final i in lehti to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -ä: lehteä.

examples.english: I am repairing a car now.
steps: Partitive presents the action as an ongoing activity without asserting that the whole task is completed.
Korjaan means “I am repairing” and works as the verb. korjaan comes from korjata: korjaa- + -n; the verb stem ends in long aa.
nyt means “now” and works as the time word. nyt is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
autoa means “car” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Add -a to auto: autoa. The ending is selected from the word’s back vowels.

examples.english: I am painting a house now.
steps: Partitive presents the action as an ongoing activity without asserting that the whole task is completed.
Maalaan means “I am painting” and works as the verb. maalaan comes from maalata: maalaa- + -n; the verb stem ends in long aa.
nyt means “now” and works as the time word. nyt is used in its displayed form here; no additional ending is needed.
taloa means “house” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep talo and add -a: talo + a = taloa.

commonMistakes: Do not translate partitive as a promise that the task will stay unfinished.
Do not confuse an activity in progress with a completed result.
